A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 20 pages in each, including Appendices A–F, provide readable text, equations, figures and tables supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original PrivacyQA and PolicyQA experiments, dialect comparisons, ablations, error analyses and translation-quality checks in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark tables, agent-feedback analyses and manual translation checks.

M1.justification: The Dialect Agent translation, Privacy Policy Agent prediction and iterative feedback procedure remain unchanged. Section 3 and Appendix B retain the same prompts and two-iteration limit.

E1.justification: Both versions use PrivacyQA sentence selection, PolicyQA answer extraction and the same synthetic English-dialect coverage generated with Multi-VALUE, including Appendix F.

E2.justification: The evaluated GPT-4o-mini, Llama 3.1 and DeepSeek-R1 comparisons retain the same zero-shot and few-shot baselines. Reference substitutions introduce no evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Reported model sizes, zero-shot and few-shot procedures, eight-example prompts, dataset processing and dataset-specific F1 metrics are unchanged in Sections 3–4.

E4.justification: The initial-versus-final and dialect-information ablations, override analysis, error examples and translation checks are retained unchanged in Tables 4–7 and 12 and Appendices A and D.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. The statistical reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout, including the appendix tables and Figure 3. For example, Table 2 retains the GPT-4o-mini multi-agent few-shot average of 0.598.

T1.justification: Section 3 retains the same formal QA task and maximum pairwise performance-disparity definition. No assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free dialect-bias mitigation, improved QA performance and up to 82% reduction in maximum cross-dialect F1 disparity.

C2.justification: Interpretations of feedback and dialect information remain unchanged, as do limitations concerning synthetic data, residual disparities, dialect metadata and English-only coverage. Appendix A and the ethical discussion are retained.

D1.justification: Actual prompt templates and dialect examples in Appendices B–C are unchanged despite surrounding prose cuts. Appendix E retains the two NVIDIA A6000 GPU disclosure; no implementation or code/data-access information is added.

R1.justification: Section 2 replaces the Chen (2023), Liu (2023a) and Xu (2023) background citations with Wang's TDAG (2025), Liu's HM-RAG (2025) and Jin's survey (2025). Sun (2023) is replaced by Jurgens (2017b), and other bibliography entries are revised. The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 revises bibliographic metadata and citation labels and removes two explanatory paragraphs surrounding Appendix B.2.2's unchanged reconsideration prompt. The remaining narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3 and Tables 1–12 retain their content and design. Reference reflow and prose cuts shift appendix text, headings and prompt boxes, particularly across pages 13–14.

improvement.justification: The methods, empirical evidence and limitations are unchanged, while Appendix B is slightly shorter. The principal revision substitutes background references, but the supplied PDFs do not establish whether those replacement sources better support the retained statements. The net quality effect is therefore uncertain.
